brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Full bases at levels 0 and 1 in two columns: piece:0,0,0, piece:0,0,1, piece:0,-1,0 and piece:0,-1,1. Covers close the top.
Four notch drawer frames, two on each storey: notch:0#-1,0#notch0, notch:1#-1,0#notch0, notch:0#1,-1#notch3 and notch:1#1,-1#notch3.

The tower is about 521 × 384 mm across and 160 mm tall, and check_build shows no rule issues and no mesh clashes. The configurator gave a tipping warning (STABILITY_TIP) when the upper drawer at (-1,0) went in. It doesn't check how much weight the tower or drawers can carry.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey storage tower with four drawers: two on each storey. Two columns of full hex bases sit side by side, at cells (0,0) and (0,-1), two levels high. The drawers are notch drawer frames that fill the spaces on either side of where the two columns meet. Covers close the top, and I ran the house rules: end caps on every open face, and joint bolts so the parts don't slide apart. check_build shows no rule issues and no mesh clashes. The tower is about 521 × 384 mm across and 160 mm tall. I added no props, so nothing shows what goes in the drawers. Two things to know: the configurator gave a tipping warning (STABILITY_TIP) when the upper drawer at (-1,0) went in, and it hasn't checked strength or how much weight the drawers can hold.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
